articles.full_text:
TWO pubs have been recognised for the quality and cleanliness of their toilets.
The Penny Black in Northwich and The Queens Arms in Winsford, both Wetherspoon pubs, received platinum plus grades in the 2026 Loo of the Year Awards, which promote high standards in public toilet facilities across the UK.
Garry Deakin, manager of The Penny Black, and The Queens Arms manager Jolene Timmis, said: "We are delighted with the gradings.
"Staff at the pubs ensure the toilets are in excellent condition at all times and it is great that this has been recognised by the inspectors."
The awards are based on unannounced inspections that assess cleanliness, maintenance, décor, accessibility, and overall management.
Facilities are graded bronze, silver, gold, platinum, platinum plus, or diamond, with unacceptable toilets not graded at all.
Becky Wall, managing director of the Loo of the Year Awards, said: "The toilets at The Penny Black and The Queens Arms have been independently assessed against the Loo of the Year Awards’ 101 criteria, recognising the standard of the facilities, their cleanliness, maintenance and overall presentation.
"The pubs thoroughly deserves their platinum plus gradings."
